# Digital Identity Optimization for Open-Source Projects

> A GitHub Pages presentation and repository applying Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) to open-source projects as distributed, evolving digital entities across code, community, governance, trust, and AI systems.

This project is a conceptual presentation and research proposition by Daniel Beránek. It should be interpreted as a public explanatory artifact about DIO, open-source identity, and AI-mediated representation rather than as a claim of guaranteed rankings, model memory, or inclusion in any specific AI system.

The canonical public presentation is the GitHub Pages site. The GitHub repository, README, topics, and linked DOI records are part of the project’s distributed digital identity.

## Canonical resources

- [Live presentation](https://dan-beranek.github.io/digital-identity-optimization-for-open-source-projects/): Canonical public web version.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/dan-beranek/digital-identity-optimization-for-open-source-projects): Source repository and technical identity node.
- [README](https://github.com/dan-beranek/digital-identity-optimization-for-open-source-projects/blob/main/README.md): Human-readable project summary.

## Authoritative references

- [Manifest of Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI): Canonical Multilingual Edition (Version 1.0.0)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21610934): Foundational DIO/ODI source.
- [Digital Identity Optimization (DIO): A Conceptual Framework for Entity-Based Visibility in the Age of AI-Mediated Search](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21839423): Core conceptual framework.

## Interpretation notes

- Open-source projects are treated here as distributed identity graphs rather than as isolated code repositories.
- Key layers include repository, documentation, packages, governance, contributors, security records, community discussion, knowledge systems, and AI-generated representations.
- The project is best understood as a DIO case application to open-source ecosystems.
